cards.title: Rising volume may signal a new trend
cards.question: What should you check before trusting a rising volume pattern?
cards.selfCheck: Compare percentage changes in trading volume with a similar stock, avoiding unusually hot or mismatched peers. A shift in volume needs price and fundamental confirmation.
cards.prompt: Explain my handwritten lesson on reading relative trading volume trends, including limitations and a practical example.

cards.title: Watch for a price–volume disconnect
cards.question: What if a stock jumps sharply without a sustained increase in relative trading activity?
cards.selfCheck: Treat a sudden price jump near a volume crossover as a hypothesis, not proof of durable demand. Look for follow-through; speculative gaps can reverse.
cards.prompt: Explain my handwritten note about large price changes near percentage trading volume crossovers, and what evidence would validate it.

cards.title: Buzz can be a clue—not confirmation
cards.question: Is rising discussion a fundamental catalyst or merely attention?
cards.selfCheck: Trace the original source, distinguish hype from new contracts or earnings, and look for measurable milestones. Popularity alone does not establish value.
cards.prompt: Explain my handwritten lesson about stock buzz, hype and the iceberg of a hidden catalyst.
